ranked_facts.concept_key: enlarged cardiac silhouette with increased pulmonary vasculature
ranked_facts.why: The presence of an enlarged cardiac silhouette with increased pulmonary vasculature is more consistent with left heart obstructive lesions, such as hypoplastic left heart syndrome, which would lead to increased pulmonary blood flow and cardiomegaly, whereas right heart obstructive lesions would typically result in decreased pulmonary blood flow.

ranked_facts.concept_key: loud single S2 with bounding pulses and wide pulse pressure
ranked_facts.why: A loud single S2 with bounding pulses and wide pulse pressure is indicative of a patent ductus arteriosus or other left-sided obstructive lesions, which would cause increased pulmonary blood flow and a wide pulse pressure, distinguishing it from right heart obstructive lesions.
